Chapter 8: The Cheese Keeps Moving—Accepting the Ongoing Nature of Change.
You know that feeling when you finally get comfortable... and then, out of nowhere, things shift again? Well, that’s exactly what happened to our little friend in the maze. He’d grown more confident after finding his new cheese, but this time, he didn’t just kick back and relax. He kept his running shoes close, stayed alert, and always checked on his cheese supply—just in case.
What he realized was pretty powerful—change isn’t just a one-and-done thing. The cheese is always on the move, and the maze? It’s full of surprises. But instead of dreading what might come next, he started to expect it. That old fear that used to freeze him in his tracks? It faded, replaced with a sense of readiness. Because now, he knew he could handle whatever twists came his way—he’d learned how to adapt.
This idea really resonated with his friends. One of them, after finally landing a new job, admitted she still felt a little anxious—what if things changed all over again? Another friend, who’d rebuilt his life after a tough divorce, wondered if he’d ever feel completely secure.
The story gave them some comfort. It’s totally normal to feel uneasy when life shifts. But here’s the good news: you can build resilience. If you see change as something that’s always happening—not just a random disruption—you stop waiting for life to “get back to normal.” Instead, you start preparing for what’s next.
So, the friends shared ideas about how to stay flexible. They talked about keeping their skills fresh, investing in relationships, and staying open to new experiences. They realized the best way to handle change isn’t to resist it, but to expect it, prepare for it, and trust that they can adapt—no matter what the maze throws their way.
